Article 7

1. The basic policy as referred to in Article 6 is elaborated in the Regional Action Plan.
2. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is integrated with the Regional Long-Term Development Plan, Regional Medium-Term Development Plan and Regional Government Work Plan documents.
3. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall at least contain:
a. programs and action activities for the protection of women and children, including women and children victims of violence;
b. regional action programs and activities to prevent all forms of violence and discrimination against women and children;
c. programs and action activities for improvement and enhancement of protection services for women and children victims of violence; and
d. programs and action activities for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.
4. Provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protecting women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development and protect women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or a child who is suspected, charged with a crime or a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color that has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PROBOLINGGO REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2019

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or the community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, therefore regulation is needed as a basis for the implementation of comprehensive and integrated protection for women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. In View of:

1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 12 of 1950 concerning the Establishment of Regency Regions within the Province of East Java (State Gazette of 1950 Number 41) as amended by Law Number 2 of 1965 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1965 Number 19, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 2730); 3. Law Number 4 of 1979 concerning Child Welfare (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1979 Number 32, Supplement to the State Gazette Number 3143); 4. Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1984 Number 29, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia 3668); 5. Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 165, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3886); 6. Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2002 Number 109, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3143) as last amended by Law Number 17 of 2016 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2016 Number 237, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5946); 7. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419); 8. Law Number 13 of 2006 concerning Protection of Witnesses and Victims (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2006 Number 64, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4635); 9. Article 29

1. Women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain counseling services from social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors.
2. Social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors as referred to in paragraph (1) are obliged to provide services to women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence in the form of providing counseling to strengthen, provide a sense of security and rehabilitation.

Article 28

1. Women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain health examination services by health care facilities in accordance with professional standards.
2. In the event that women and children who are victims, witnesses, and perpetrators of violence require treatment, health workers are obliged to provide health recovery and rehabilitation services.
3. The provision of health recovery and rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 36

1. Supervision as referred to in Article 35 shall be conducted on:
a. the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children; and
b. the fulfillment of guidelines and minimum service standards in the implementation of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children who are victims of violence.
2. Supervision shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year and the results shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.

Article 21

Protection of women and child victims of violence includes:
a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

Article 20

1. Every woman and child who becomes a witness or perpetrator of violence has the right to receive information, protection, rehabilitation, confidential handling, psychological and legal assistance, as well as fulfillment of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member or as a community member.
2. Fulfillment of rights as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 18

1. In the event that women and child victims of violence require continuous handling, then women and child victims of violence have the right to stay in a safe house or alternative residence.
2. Continuous handling as referred to in paragraph (1) is handling at the rehabilitation stage, whether carried out by PPT, individuals, non-governmental organizations, or by the community.

Article 26

1. Assistance shall be carried out by individuals or institutions that have expertise in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence, perpetrators and witnesses.
2. Provisions regarding assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 27

For the purpose of recovery, women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence may obtain services from:
a. Social institutions (groups or institutions whose scope is on women and children) and or;
b. Social workers (Individuals who have the competence to carry out recovery or rehabilitation) namely:
1\. Nurses
2\. Health workers

Paragraph 4

Scope

Article 19

1. Safe houses as referred to in Article 18 paragraph (1) provide temporary safe places and/or shelter for victims of violence until their rights are restored.
2. The operation and/or management of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the relevant Agency.
3. Provisions regarding the operation of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (2) are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO,

Considering:

b. regional action programs and activities to prevent all forms of violence and discrimination against women and children;
c. programs and action activities for improvement and enhancement of protection services for women and children victims of violence; and
d. programs and action activities for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protecting women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development and protect women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or a child who is suspected, charged with a crime or a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color that has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 36

1. Supervision as referred to in Article 35 shall be conducted on:
a. the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children; and
b. the fulfillment of guidelines and minimum service standards in the implementation of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children who are victims of violence.
2. Supervision shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year and the results shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.

Article 29

1. Women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain counseling services from social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors.
2. Social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors as referred to in paragraph (1) are obliged to provide services to women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence in the form of providing counseling to strengthen, provide a sense of security and rehabilitation.

Article 28

1. Women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain health examination services by health care facilities in accordance with professional standards.
2. In the event that women and children who are victims, witnesses, and perpetrators of violence require treatment, health workers are obliged to provide health recovery and rehabilitation services.
3. The provision of health recovery and rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 21

Protection of women and child victims of violence includes:
a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

Article 20

1. Every woman and child who becomes a witness or perpetrator of violence has the right to receive information, protection, rehabilitation, confidential handling, psychological and legal assistance, as well as fulfillment of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member or as a community member.
2. Fulfillment of rights as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protecting women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development and protect women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or a child who is suspected, charged with a crime or a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color that has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PROBOLINGGO REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2019

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or the community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, therefore regulation is needed as a basis for the implementation of comprehensive and integrated protection for women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. Article 28

1. Women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain health examination services by health care facilities in accordance with professional standards.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protecting women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development and protect women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or a child who is suspected, charged with a crime or a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color that has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PROBOLINGGO REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2019

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or the community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, therefore regulation is needed as a basis for the implementation of comprehensive and integrated protection for women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development and protect women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or a child who is suspected, charged with a crime or a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color that has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 28

1. Women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain health examination services by health care facilities in accordance with professional standards.
2. In the event that women and children who are victims, witnesses, and perpetrators of violence require treatment, health workers are obliged to provide health recovery and rehabilitation services.
3. The provision of health recovery and rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 29

1. Women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain counseling services from social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors.
2. Social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors as referred to in paragraph (1) are obliged to provide services to women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence in the form of providing counseling to strengthen, provide a sense of security and rehabilitation.

Article 26

1. Assistance shall be carried out by individuals or institutions that have expertise in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence, perpetrators and witnesses.
2. Provisions regarding assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 18

1. In the event that women and child victims of violence require continuous handling, then women and child victims of violence have the right to stay in a safe house or alternative residence.
2. Continuous handling as referred to in paragraph (1) is handling at the rehabilitation stage, whether carried out by PPT, individuals, non-governmental organizations, or by the community.

Article 20

1. Every woman and child who becomes a witness or perpetrator of violence has the right to receive information, protection, rehabilitation, confidential handling, psychological and legal assistance, as well as fulfillment of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member or as a community member.
2. Fulfillment of rights as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 28

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protecting women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development and protect women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or a child who is suspected, charged with a crime or a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color that has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PROBOLINGGO REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2019

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or the community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, therefore regulation is needed as a basis for the implementation of comprehensive and integrated protection for women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. CHAPTER I

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.

3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protecting women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development and protect women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or a child who is suspected, charged with a crime or a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color that has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or the community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, therefore regulation is needed as a basis for the implementation of comprehensive and integrated protection for women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. REGIONAL REGULATION OF PROBOLINGGO REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2019

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or the community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, therefore regulation is needed as a basis for the implementation of comprehensive and integrated protection for women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. In View of:

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or the community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, therefore regulation is needed as a basis for the implementation of comprehensive and integrated protection for women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color that has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 9

1. The Regent is obliged to implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in an integrated manner in order to fulfill the rights of women and children in the Region.
2. In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (1), the Agency coordinates with regional apparatus organizations, law enforcement officials and the community.

CHAPTER III

Article 4

The Regional Government is obliged to implement the protection of women and children.
